gameSystem.name: ⚔️ The Long War: List Builder

categoryEntries.name: Warlord
categoryEntries.comment: Hidden semantic marker placed on a *selected Warlord designation* rather than on all eligible Characters. The Game System's live counter counts this category; the active faction force enforces the over-one limit. Do not attach to the parent unit merely because it can become Warlord.

categoryEntries.name: Psyker
categoryEntries.comment: Semantic unit-level eligibility marker for the Psyker (X) SPECIAL RULE, not a literal datasheet keyword. Only attach to a unit when its selected configuration actually grants Psyker (X); do not list Special Rules as user-facing profiles. Used by Iron Warriors' Mark of Chaos restriction (unit-local).

selectionEntries.name: About Warsmith's Listbuilder

rules.name: A fancy notepad, not a rules engine
rules.description:
The listbuilder is intended to replace a notepad, not The Long War rules PDFs. It quickly and simply records the choices that make up an army and catches illegal list construction. It does not reproduce every unit special rule, weapon profile, or procedural rule from the rulebook and army rules PDFs.

Players are expected to consult The Long War rulebook and the relevant army rules during list construction.

rules.name: Not every legal option needs its own button
rules.description:
The listbuilder is intended to make common choices quick, rather than give every legal option equal prominence. Some uncommon squad sizes or loadout combinations may therefore not be represented. Their absence does not make them illegal; The Long War rules PDFs remain authoritative.

When players actually make use of an uncommon option, it can be added accordingly.

selectionEntries.comment: Default-inserted, informational player guidance only. Keep user-facing text concise and free of internal engineering notes. This is not an army-legalization or source-rules engine.

selectionEntries.name: Crusade Detachment Mandatory HQ: 0/1
selectionEntries.comment: Default-inserted dynamic name: 0/1 -> 1/1 via roster-wide primary HQ count. A visible completion objective, not an automatic missing-HQ error or a maximum-slot constraint. Replacing its primary category would change the count. The active faction force checks if this Configuration entry is deleted.

selectionEntries.name: Crusade Detachment Mandatory Troops: 0/2
selectionEntries.comment: Default-inserted dynamic name: 0/2 -> 1/2 -> 2/2 via roster-wide primary Troops count. Capped as progress, not as inventory. Deliberately no red error merely for an incomplete newly created army. Deletion protection lives on the active faction force.

selectionEntries.name: 👑 Mandatory Warlord: 0/1
selectionEntries.comment: Default-inserted dynamic name: 0/1 -> 1/1 when a selected Warlord checkbox contributes the hidden Warlord category. No red error for an incomplete roster. Faction force enforces Warlord max-one and protects against deletion of this Configuration entry.

gameSystem.comment:
THE LONG WAR / GAME SYSTEM — CURRENT-STATE HANDOFF (Iron Warriors start, 2026-10-31)
AUTHORITY: This Game System defines reusable New Recruit presentation/validation infrastructure; the Long War core rules, faction codices, Allegiances and Rites are authoritative for actual legality. Do not import Reforged gameplay rules merely because we reuse its user interface and proven catalogue patterns.
RESPONSIBILITIES: This Game System owns the primary Battlefield Role categories (HQ, Troops, Elite, Dedicated Transport, Fast Attack, Heavy Support, Flyers, Fortifications, Lord of War), reusable unit-type presentation categories, hidden 'Warlord' marker and reusable hidden 'Psyker' eligibility marker, the '🏷️ Keywords' profile type, and default-inserted Configuration information. The faction catalogue owns actual units, faction-specific Allegiances/Rites, shared keyword categories, and its force-wide validation. There is no separate Crusade Detachment selection or permanent force-organisation chart.
CONVENTIONS: Configuration sort positions are 10 Allegiance / 20 Rite / 30 Mandatory HQ / 40 Mandatory Troops / 50 Mandatory Warlord / 90 Updated / 100 About; preserve ordering when adding new objectives. Primary category determines the player's unit browser heading and which force-organisation slot a selection counts toward. Type and semantic keywords are secondary categories, independent of the displayed emoji-bearing Keywords profile. Keep real keyword names unadorned in hidden categories; emojis belong in presentation only. Different Battlefield Role entries may eventually share a hidden 'Counts as' identity, but never replace slot accounting with it.
PLAYER UX: Configuration shows actionable goals (mandatory HQ/Troops/Warlord progress), not standing maximum limits. Role ceilings and conditional restrictions raise three-sentence problem/rule/correction errors when violated; do not hard-gate or silently remove selected units. Mandatory counters are intentionally informational: a fresh unfinished roster must not start with red errors. Faction force-level checks protect against deletion of essential Configuration entries, but informational About/Updated entries do not need those safeguards.
KEYWORD NUMBER: The Long War core rules say singular and plural forms of a keyword are equivalent. Choose a sensible canonical semantic-category identity per concept for new work, without touching existing stable IDs merely for spelling (e.g. Veterans, Chaos Lord). 'Psyker' here encodes the Psyker (X) special-rule eligibility for validation only; do not add a player-facing Special Rules profile.
MAINTENANCE: Preserve existing IDs, native (None) option semantics, stable selected entries, selection topology and visual ordering. Document only non-obvious design decisions, dependencies, deliberate source deviations, engine quirks and verified/untested behavior. Do not repeat ordinary unit points, category names, or option text in comments. No Special Rules/ability encyclopedia in the roster: the PDF stays authoritative.
STATUS: The early V3.3 force-org test scaffold was reported working in New Recruit. Later Warlord, configuration-integrity, polymorphic, keyword and dual-claw behaviors have static checks, not comprehensive live confirmation.
